title: Matching labeling Fourier weight
statement: Let $n,k,q$ be natural numbers, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, and let a graph matching labeling consist of a perfect matching in the complete $q$-partite graph with $k$ vertices per part and a compatible labeling by an $n$-element set. Its Fourier weight for $f$ is the product, over the parts, of the absolute values of the Fourier coefficients indexed by the sets of labels attained in those parts.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is real-valued on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
The graph matching labeling contains a perfect matching in the complete $q$-partite graph with $k$ vertices per part
The labeling takes values in an $n$-element set
The labeling is compatible with the matching
